context: Wheel's execution backend is POSIX: a constant sh wrapper, setsid process groups, POSIX FIFOs for the control plane, and GNU coreutils assumptions. SECURITY-MODEL.md:1239 states a non-POSIX platform fails closed at seam construction.
decision_body: Windows is supported only through WSL2. No native Windows process backend is planned; the sandbox is not the blocker. macOS is supported at the core level (POSIX) with Seatbelt as a separate sandbox backend that may lag Linux. The sandbox is a policy layer (filesystem + network policy) with per-platform backends, so adding a platform adds a backend rather than changing the CLI or Lua surfaces.
title: Platform support: Linux and macOS native, Windows via WSL2 only

context: bitty-ai currently ships skeletons (bitty-ai-endpoint stops at the admit point; bitty-ai-host has no transport or provider wiring), while the working provider path lives in Wheel (lua/wheel/provider.lua, ~3.1k lines: curl transport, streaming, thinking gears, six provider templates). Without a recorded boundary both sides can implement provider authentication and model selection, producing two authorities and divergent behaviour.
decision_body: Split: bitty-ai owns the ai.* method contract (method resolution, scope/consent/deadline gates, exact-byte binding, publication state). Wheel owns transport and presentation of model calls (HTTP/streaming, retries, thinking gears, provider templates, CLI flags). A future independent repository may own the model catalogue/provider registry; until then Wheel is the single implementation and must not grow a second authorization path, and bitty-ai must not add provider transport.
title: Provider/model boundary: bitty-ai owns ai.* semantics, Wheel owns transport

context: The first sandbox landed as opt-in (--sandbox) because the sandbox has no HOME and would present an empty Wheel config, credentials, and approval state. That contradicts the fail-closed posture the design called for: a bare scripts/wheel stays unconfined, so isolation only protects sessions the operator remembers to wrap. Owner reviewed the trade-off and chose the middle position over both the opt-in status quo and an empty-config default.
decision_body: wheel run enters the OS sandbox by default. The host Wheel config directory is mounted read-only so configuration, provider definitions, and agent/role settings are usable; nothing inside the sandbox can mutate them. Credentials never enter the sandbox: they are injected at the host relay for WHEEL_SANDBOX_AUTH_HOSTS destinations only. Writable session state (sessions, approvals, trust store, traces) moves to the per-session cache directory, or degrades explicitly when it cannot be written. --no-sandbox is the single explicit opt-out and must be visible in help output and in SECURITY-MODEL.md. wheel ask and wheel chat follow the same rule. Providers require proxy mode; netless mode stays available for offline work.
title: Default sandbox posture: wheel run is sandboxed unless --no-sandbox
